accessible.ex: The library is accessible to all students.

accounts.en: records that let you use a website
accounts.ex: You need an account to buy tickets online.
accounts.zh: 帳戶（set up accounts：建立帳戶）

across.es: en todo; a lo largo de

against.en: against the law: not allowed by law

age.ex: She started school at the age of four.

aged.ex: Children aged five can join the class.

already.ex: The train had already left when we arrived.

also.ex: She speaks French and also Spanish.

an.en: one; any (also part of the name An Post)

approximately.en: close to a number, not exact
approximately.ex: The trip takes approximately three hours.

around.ex: Around fifty people came to the party.

assured.en: told someone firmly that something is true
assured.ex: The pilot assured us the flight would be safe.

at.en: in or near a place or time

attributed.ex: He attributed his success to hard work.
attributed.ja: 〜のせいにした（attribute A to B）

attributing.en: saying something is caused by something else
attributing.ex: Doctors attribute her recovery to early treatment.

available.en: able to be used or obtained

average.ex: The average price of a house rose again.

aviation.ex: He has worked in aviation for twenty years.

awards.en: shares given to staff as part of pay
awards.ex: Senior staff received large share awards.

be.en: to exist or have a quality

big.ex: It was a big decision for the family.

bigger.ex: Our new flat is bigger than the old one.

blunt.ex: Exam results are a blunt way to judge schools.
blunt.zh: 粗略的（blunt instrument：粗糙的工具）

broadens.ex: The river broadens as it reaches the sea.

called.ex: This small town is called Bray.

career.en: the jobs a person does over their working life
career.ex: She had a long career in teaching.

cautions.ex: The doctor cautions against eating too much salt.

central.en: part of the name Central Statistics Office
central.zh: 中央的（Central Statistics Office：中央統計局）

chiefly.ex: The town is chiefly known for its castle.

companies.en: businesses that make or sell things
companies.ex: Many companies let staff work from home.

company.ex: The company employs two hundred people.

consequently.ex: It rained all day; consequently, the match was cancelled.

considerable.ex: The project needs a considerable amount of money.

example.en: The project took a considerable amount of time.
example.zh: 這個專案花了相當多的時間。

note.meaning: 相當大的、可觀的；文中指各公司數據之間差異很大。
note.usage: 形容詞，多放在名詞前，如 considerable variation/amount；副詞 considerably 修飾比較級。

noteEn.meaning: large in size, amount or importance.

noteEs.exampleTr: El proyecto llevó una cantidad considerable de tiempo.
noteEs.meaning: Bastante grande o importante; aquí, la variación entre empresas es grande.
noteEs.usage: Adjetivo antes del sustantivo: 'considerable variation', 'a considerable amount of'.

noteHi.exampleTr: इस परियोजना में काफ़ी समय लगा।
noteHi.meaning: काफ़ी बड़ा या उल्लेखनीय; यहाँ कंपनियों के आँकड़ों में काफ़ी अंतर है।
noteHi.usage: विशेषण, संज्ञा से पहले: considerable variation, a considerable amount of।

noteJa.exampleTr: そのプロジェクトにはかなりの時間がかかった。
noteJa.meaning: かなりの、相当な。記事では企業間のデータのばらつきが大きいことを表す。
noteJa.usage: 形容詞で名詞の前に置く。considerable variation、a considerable amount of など。

noteKo.meaning: 상당한, 꽤 큰. 기사에서는 기업 간 수치 차이가 크다는 뜻이다.
noteKo.usage: 형용사로 명사 앞에 쓴다. considerable variation, a considerable amount of 등.

construction.en: the industry of building houses and roads
construction.ex: Construction of the bridge began in May.

consultancy.en: a company that gives expert advice
consultancy.ex: He set up a small IT consultancy.

contrasts.ex: There are sharp contrasts between city and country life.

course.ex: Over the course of the day, the weather improved.
course.ja: 過程（over the course of：〜の間に）
course.zh: 過程（over the course of：在…期間）

covering.ex: The report, covering ten years, is long.

currently.ex: She is currently living in Cork.

data.en: facts and numbers collected for study
data.ex: The app collects data about your sleep.

date.ex: What is the date of the meeting?

deadline.en: the latest time something must be done
deadline.ex: The deadline for the essay is Friday.

defined.ex: Poverty is often defined as living on very little money.

difference.en: the amount by which things are not the same
difference.ex: There is a big difference in price between the two phones.

differences.en: ways things are not the same
differences.ex: There are big price differences between shops.

disclose.ex: Companies must disclose their profits every year.

example.en: The company refused to disclose the details of the deal.
example.zh: 公司拒絕透露這筆交易的細節。

note.meaning: 公開、揭露（資訊）；文中指企業必須在網站上公布薪資數據。
note.usage: 及物動詞，常接 information/details/figures；disclose sth to sb；名詞 disclosure。

noteEn.meaning: to make information known to the public or to someone.

noteEs.exampleTr: La empresa se negó a revelar los detalles del acuerdo.
noteEs.meaning: Revelar o hacer pública una información; aquí, las empresas deben publicar sus cifras.
noteEs.usage: Verbo transitivo; 'disclose information/figures', 'disclose sth to sb'. Sustantivo: disclosure.

noteHi.exampleTr: कंपनी ने सौदे का विवरण बताने से इनकार कर दिया।
noteHi.meaning: जानकारी सार्वजनिक करना या बताना; यहाँ कंपनियों को अपने आँकड़े प्रकाशित करने हैं।
noteHi.usage: disclose information/figures, disclose sth to sb आम हैं; संज्ञा disclosure।

noteJa.exampleTr: その会社は取引の詳細を明かすことを拒んだ。
noteJa.meaning: （情報を）公開する、開示する。記事では企業が賃金データを公表することを指す。
noteJa.usage: 他動詞。disclose information/figures、disclose sth to sb の形。名詞は disclosure。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 회사는 거래의 세부 사항을 밝히기를 거부했다.
noteKo.meaning: (정보를) 공개하다, 밝히다. 기사에서는 기업이 임금 수치를 공개해야 한다는 뜻이다.
noteKo.usage: 타동사로 disclose information/figures, disclose sth to sb 형태. 명사형은 disclosure.

disclosures.ex: The disclosures led to a public inquiry.

disparities.ex: There are big health disparities between rich and poor areas.

collocations: a disparity between A and B

example.en: There is a huge disparity between rich and poor areas of the city.
example.zh: 這座城市的富裕區和貧困區之間存在巨大差距。

note.meaning: 差距、不均等；文中指男女員工之間收入的平均差距。
note.usage: 可數名詞，常用 disparity between A and B 或 disparity in + 名詞（如 pay/income）。

noteEn.meaning: a big difference between two things, often seen as unfair.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'a disparity between A and B', 'pay disparity'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Hay una enorme disparidad entre las zonas ricas y pobres de la ciudad.
noteEs.meaning: Diferencia o desigualdad notable; aquí, entre los ingresos de hombres y mujeres.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo contable; se usa 'disparity between A and B' o 'disparity in pay/income'.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर के अमीर और ग़रीब इलाकों के बीच भारी असमानता है।
noteHi.meaning: दो चीज़ों के बीच बड़ा अंतर या असमानता; यहाँ पुरुषों और महिलाओं की कमाई का अंतर।
noteHi.usage: disparity between A and B, disparity in pay/income आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: その都市の裕福な地域と貧しい地域の間には大きな格差がある。
noteJa.meaning: 格差、不均衡。記事では男女の従業員の平均収入の差を指す。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。disparity between A and B、disparity in pay/income の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 도시의 부유한 지역과 가난한 지역 사이에는 엄청난 격차가 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 격차, 불균형. 기사에서는 남녀 직원 간 평균 소득의 차이를 뜻한다.
noteKo.usage: 가산명사로 disparity between A and B, disparity in pay/income 형태로 자주 쓴다.

disparity.ex: The disparity between their salaries is huge.

collocations: a disparity between A and B

example.en: There is a huge disparity between rich and poor areas of the city.
example.zh: 這座城市的富裕區和貧困區之間存在巨大差距。

note.meaning: 差距、不均等；文中指男女員工之間收入的平均差距。
note.usage: 可數名詞，常用 disparity between A and B 或 disparity in + 名詞（如 pay/income）。

noteEn.meaning: a big difference between two things, often seen as unfair.
noteEn.usage: Common: 'a disparity between A and B', 'pay disparity'.

noteEs.exampleTr: Hay una enorme disparidad entre las zonas ricas y pobres de la ciudad.
noteEs.meaning: Diferencia o desigualdad notable; aquí, entre los ingresos de hombres y mujeres.
noteEs.usage: Sustantivo contable; se usa 'disparity between A and B' o 'disparity in pay/income'.

noteHi.exampleTr: शहर के अमीर और ग़रीब इलाकों के बीच भारी असमानता है।
noteHi.meaning: दो चीज़ों के बीच बड़ा अंतर या असमानता; यहाँ पुरुषों और महिलाओं की कमाई का अंतर।
noteHi.usage: disparity between A and B, disparity in pay/income आम प्रयोग हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: その都市の裕福な地域と貧しい地域の間には大きな格差がある。
noteJa.meaning: 格差、不均衡。記事では男女の従業員の平均収入の差を指す。
noteJa.usage: 可算名詞。disparity between A and B、disparity in pay/income の形でよく使う。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 도시의 부유한 지역과 가난한 지역 사이에는 엄청난 격차가 있다.
noteKo.meaning: 격차, 불균형. 기사에서는 남녀 직원 간 평균 소득의 차이를 뜻한다.
noteKo.usage: 가산명사로 disparity between A and B, disparity in pay/income 형태로 자주 쓴다.

does.en: used to form questions and negatives

domain.en: in the public domain: available for everyone to see
domain.ex: The report is now in the public domain.
domain.zh: 領域（in the public domain：公開的）

dáil.en: the lower house of Ireland's parliament
dáil.hi: डाइल (आयरलैंड की संसद का निचला सदन)
dáil.ja: ドイル（アイルランド下院）

earn.ex: She earns more than her brother.

economy.en: the money and business system of a country
economy.ex: Tourism is important for the local economy.

example.en: The teacher emphasised the importance of reading every day.
example.zh: 老師強調了每天閱讀的重要性。

note.meaning: 強調；文中指專家特別指出薪資差距並不代表同工不同酬。
note.usage: 及物動詞，可接名詞或 that 子句；英式 emphasise，美式 emphasize；名詞 emphasis。

noteEn.meaning: to say something strongly to show it is important.

noteEs.exampleTr: El profesor destacó la importancia de leer todos los días.
noteEs.meaning: Destacar o subrayar algo; aquí, la experta insiste en que la brecha no mide igual salario.
noteEs.usage: Verbo transitivo; se usa con 'that' o 'emphasise the importance of'. Sustantivo: emphasis.

noteHi.exampleTr: शिक्षक ने रोज़ पढ़ने के महत्व पर ज़ोर दिया।
noteHi.meaning: किसी बात पर ज़ोर देना; यहाँ विशेषज्ञ स्पष्ट करती हैं कि अंतर समान काम के वेतन का माप नहीं।
noteHi.usage: सकर्मक क्रिया; emphasise that..., emphasise the importance of आम हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: 先生は毎日読書することの大切さを強調した。
noteJa.meaning: 強調する。記事では専門家が格差は同一労働の賃金差ではないと強調することを指す。
noteJa.usage: 他動詞で名詞や that 節をとる。名詞は emphasis、米式綴りは emphasize。

noteKo.exampleTr: 선생님은 매일 독서하는 것의 중요성을 강조했다.
noteKo.meaning: 강조하다. 기사에서는 전문가가 격차가 동일 노동 임금 차이가 아니라고 강조하는 것을 뜻한다.
noteKo.usage: 타동사로 명사나 that절을 취한다. 명사형은 emphasis, 미국식 철자는 emphasize.

employees.en: people who work for a company

employer.en: a person or company that pays workers
employer.ex: The employer agreed to raise wages.

employers.en: people or companies that pay workers
employers.ex: Employers must pay into workers' pensions.

enabling.ex: New tools are enabling faster repairs.

end.en: the last part of a period of time
end.ex: We pay the rent at the end of each month.
end.ja: 終わり（by the end of：〜末までに）
end.zh: 末尾（by the end of：在…之前）

enshrined.ex: Free speech is enshrined in the constitution.

example.en: Freedom of speech is enshrined in the constitution.
example.zh: 言論自由明文載於憲法之中。

note.meaning: （將權利、原則）正式載入法律或文件中；文中指同工同酬已明文寫進法律。
note.usage: 常用被動 be enshrined in law/the constitution。

noteEn.meaning: to officially protect a right or idea by writing it into law.

noteEs.exampleTr: La libertad de expresión está consagrada en la constitución.
noteEs.meaning: Consagrar un derecho o principio en una ley; aquí, el igual salario ya está en la ley.
noteEs.usage: Suele usarse en pasiva: 'be enshrined in law/the constitution'.

noteHi.exampleTr: अभिव्यक्ति की स्वतंत्रता संविधान में निहित है।
noteHi.meaning: किसी अधिकार या सिद्धांत को कानून में औपचारिक रूप से दर्ज करना; यहाँ समान वेतन कानून में है।
noteHi.usage: अक्सर कर्मवाच्य में: be enshrined in law/the constitution।

noteJa.exampleTr: 言論の自由は憲法に明記されている。
noteJa.meaning: （権利・原則を）法律などに正式に明記する。記事では同一賃金がすでに法律で定められていることを指す。
noteJa.usage: 受動態 be enshrined in law/the constitution でよく使う。

noteKo.meaning: (권리·원칙을) 법 등에 공식적으로 명시하다. 기사에서는 동일 임금이 이미 법에 규정되어 있다는 뜻이다.
noteKo.usage: 주로 수동태 be enshrined in law/the constitution으로 쓴다.

equal.en: the same in amount or value

equality.en: fair treatment with the same rights for all
equality.ex: The group campaigns for equality between men and women.
equality.zh: 平等（Minister for Equality：平等部長）

equity.ex: Staff receive equity as part of their pay.

equity-based.en: paid in the form of company shares
equity-based.ex: Many tech workers receive equity-based bonuses.

exhibit.en: to show a feature or quality
exhibit.ex: Some patients exhibit no symptoms at all.

example.en: The patient began to exhibit signs of recovery.
example.zh: 病人開始出現康復的跡象。

note.meaning: 顯示出、呈現（某種特徵）；文中指男性主導的產業往往呈現較大的薪資差距。
note.usage: 及物動詞，正式用法，常接 signs/features/behaviour；也可指展覽作品。

noteEn.meaning: to show a feature or quality clearly.

noteEs.exampleTr: El paciente empezó a mostrar signos de recuperación.
noteEs.meaning: Mostrar o presentar una característica; aquí, ciertos sectores muestran brechas mayores.
noteEs.usage: Verbo formal; común en 'exhibit signs of' o 'exhibit a pattern'. También 'exponer' obras.

noteHi.exampleTr: मरीज़ में ठीक होने के लक्षण दिखने लगे।
noteHi.meaning: कोई गुण या लक्षण दिखाना; यहाँ कुछ क्षेत्रों में बड़ा वेतन अंतर दिखता है।
noteHi.usage: औपचारिक सकर्मक क्रिया; exhibit signs of, exhibit a pattern आम हैं।

noteJa.exampleTr: その患者は回復の兆しを見せ始めた。
noteJa.meaning: （特徴などを）示す、見せる。記事では一部の業界で格差が大きく表れることを指す。
noteJa.usage: 改まった他動詞。exhibit signs of、exhibit a pattern などで使う。「展示する」の意味もある。

noteKo.exampleTr: 그 환자는 회복의 징후를 보이기 시작했다.
noteKo.meaning: (특징 등을) 보이다, 나타내다. 기사에서는 일부 업종에서 격차가 더 크게 나타난다는 뜻이다.
noteKo.usage: 격식 있는 타동사로 exhibit signs of, exhibit a pattern 등으로 쓴다. '전시하다'의 뜻도 있다.

expert.en: a person with special knowledge or skill
expert.ex: We asked an expert to check the old painting.

expose.en: to show something that was hidden
expose.ex: The report exposed problems in the hospital.

fare.en: to do well or badly in a situation
fare.ex: Small shops fared badly during the crisis.
fare.ja: （うまく・まずく）やっていく
fare.zh: 表現；情況（fare worst：表現最差）

favour.en: in someone's favour: to their advantage
favour.ex: The score was 3–1 in our favour.

female.ex: The company hired more female engineers this year.

few.en: a small number of (how few: how small a number)
few.ja: ほとんどない（how few：いかに少ないか）

figure.en: a number; an amount shown in data
figure.ex: The official figure was lower than expected.

figures.ex: The latest figures show a rise.

finance.en: the business of banking and money
finance.ex: He got a job in finance after university.

for.en: used to show purpose or who gets something

from.en: showing where something starts or comes

furthermore.ex: The flat is cheap; furthermore, it is near work.

gap.ex: The gap between rich and poor is growing.

gaps.ex: Some sectors have much wider pay gaps.

gauge.ex: It is hard to gauge public opinion.

example.en: It is hard to gauge how people will react to the news.
example.zh: 很難判斷人們會如何回應這則消息。

note.meaning: 衡量、評估；文中指此指標並不能衡量同工是否同酬。
note.usage: 及物動詞，常接 reaction/opinion/effect；也可作名詞「量尺、指標」。注意拼字 gauge。

noteEs.exampleTr: Es difícil calibrar cómo reaccionará la gente ante la noticia.
noteEs.meaning: Medir o evaluar algo; aquí, el indicador no mide igual salario por igual trabajo.
noteEs.usage: Verbo transitivo; 'gauge public opinion', 'difficult to gauge'. También es sustantivo.

noteHi.exampleTr: यह आँकना मुश्किल है कि लोग इस ख़बर पर कैसी प्रतिक्रिया देंगे।
noteHi.meaning: किसी चीज़ को मापना या आँकना; यहाँ यह माप समान काम के समान वेतन को नहीं आँकता।
noteHi.usage: सकर्मक क्रिया; gauge public opinion, difficult to gauge आम हैं; संज्ञा भी है।

noteJa.exampleTr: 人々がそのニュースにどう反応するかを見極めるのは難しい。
noteJa.meaning: 測る、評価する。記事ではこの指標が同一労働同一賃金を測るものではないことを指す。
noteJa.usage: 他動詞。gauge public opinion、difficult to gauge など。名詞で「計器、尺度」も。

noteKo.exampleTr: 사람들이 그 소식에 어떻게 반응할지 가늠하기 어렵다.
noteKo.meaning: 측정하다, 가늠하다. 기사에서는 이 지표가 동일 노동 동일 임금을 측정하지 않는다는 뜻이다.
noteKo.usage: 타동사로 gauge public opinion, difficult to gauge 등. 명사로 '계기, 척도'도 된다.

gender.ex: Jobs should be open to all, regardless of gender.
gender.zh: 性別（gender pay gap：性別薪資差距）

get.ex: You get a free coffee with every sandwich.

government.en: the group of people who run a country
government.ex: The government will build new schools.

grows.ex: The town grows bigger every year.

have.en: to own or hold; also helps form tenses

headcount.en: the number of people working somewhere
headcount.ex: The firm plans to cut its headcount by ten percent.

held.ex: The top post is held by a woman for the first time.

higher.ex: Prices are higher in the city centre.

hold.en: to have a job or position
hold.ex: She holds a senior post at the bank.

how.ex: Show me how this machine works.

hr.en: human resources; managing a company's staff
hr.ex: Please send your CV to the HR department.

identical.ex: The two houses look almost identical.

in.en: inside; at a place or time

indicate.en: to show or be a sign of

indicating.ex: The results are positive, indicating real progress.

individual.ex: Each individual school sets its own rules.

instrument.en: a tool or way of doing something
instrument.ex: Taxes are an instrument of government policy.
instrument.zh: 工具；手段（blunt instrument：粗糙的工具）

job.ex: He found a new job in Dublin.

jobs.ex: The new factory will create 500 jobs.

larger.ex: They moved to a larger house.

launched.en: started or made public for the first time
launched.ex: The new website was launched in May.
launched.ja: 発表された；開始された

law.en: a rule made by a government
law.ex: The new law protects workers' rights.

legal.ex: She asked a lawyer for legal advice.

less.ex: This road is less busy at night.

lets.ex: My mum lets me stay up late on Fridays.

level.en: a scale, e.g. national or local
level.ex: The rule applies at local level too.

paragraphs: A new Government website shows how much men and women earn at Irish companies.
In Ireland, women earn about 8.3% less than men on average. This is called the gender pay gap.
Big employers must put their numbers on the website by the end of November. This means all employers with more than 50 workers. About 410 reports are already there.
The numbers are very different between companies. At Meta, the gap is 26.5%. At An Post, women earn a little more than men.
The gap is bigger for older workers. For people aged 50 to 59, it is 16.7%.
One expert says the gap does not mean women get less money for the same job. It shows that more men have the top jobs.
A new Government website now lets people see whether women earn less than men at Irish companies. On average, women in Ireland earn 8.3% less than men. This difference is called the gender pay gap.

By the end of November, every employer with more than 50 staff must publish its pay gap figures on the website. The Minister for Equality, Norma Foley, says the new figures for 2026 will be online by then. About 1,000 employers have already set up accounts, and 410 reports for 2025 are available.
The results are very different from one company to another. Meta's Irish company reports a gap of 26.5%, while at An Post women earn slightly more than men on average.
Official figures also show that the gap grows with age. For workers aged 50 to 59, it reaches 16.7%.

Michelle McDonagh, an HR expert at the company Adare, says the gap does not show that women are paid less for the same job, because that is already against the law. Instead, it mostly shows that fewer women have senior jobs.

A new public website is revealing how much more men earn than women at individual Irish employers. Nationally, the gender pay gap, which is the average difference in pay between all men and all women at work, stands at 8.3%.

By the end of November, all organisations with more than 50 employees must publish their gender pay gap data on the portal. Minister for Equality Norma Foley has told the Dáil that the 2026 figures will be available by then. Around 1,000 employers have already registered, and 410 reports covering 2025 have been published.

The figures vary widely. Meta Platforms Ireland reported a gap of 26.5%, which it linked mainly to technical roles and share-based pay, while An Post recorded a gap of minus 4.85%, meaning women there earn slightly more on average.
Data from the Central Statistics Office also shows the gap widening with age, reaching 16.7% among workers aged 50 to 59. Sectors such as construction, aviation and finance tend to have larger gaps.

Michelle McDonagh of the HR consultancy Adare points out that the gap is not a measure of equal pay for the same work, which is already required by law. Rather, she says, it largely reflects how few women hold senior positions.

A new Government portal is shining a light on pay disparities between men and women at individual Irish employers. Across the economy, the gender pay gap, meaning the average difference in earnings between all male and all female workers, currently sits at 8.3%.

Every organisation with a headcount of more than 50 is obliged to disclose its figures on the site by the end of November. Minister for Equality Norma Foley has assured the Dáil that the 2026 data will be publicly accessible by that deadline. Some 1,000 employers have already signed up, and 410 reports for 2025 are in the public domain.

The disclosures expose stark contrasts. Meta Platforms Ireland posted a gap of 26.5%, attributing it chiefly to technical roles and equity awards, whereas An Post recorded a negative gap of 4.85%, tilting marginally in women's favour.

Official statistics also reveal that the gap broadens over the course of a career, peaking at 16.7% among those aged 50 to 59. Male-dominated sectors such as construction, aviation and finance typically fare worst.

Michelle McDonagh of the HR consultancy Adare cautions that the metric is a blunt instrument: it does not gauge equal pay for equal work, which is already enshrined in law, but rather mirrors the under-representation of women in senior roles.

A newly launched Government website is enabling the public to scrutinise pay differences between men and women at individual Irish organisations. At national level, the gender pay gap, defined as the average disparity in earnings between all male and all female employees, currently stands at 8.3%.

All employers with more than 50 staff are required to publish their data on the portal by the end of November. According to the Minister for Equality, Norma Foley, the 2026 figures will be accessible by that date. Approximately 1,000 employers have already registered, and 410 reports relating to 2025 have been published.

The data reveal considerable variation. Meta Platforms Ireland reported a gap of 26.5%, which it attributed predominantly to technical positions and equity-based remuneration, whereas An Post recorded a negative gap of 4.85%, indicating marginally higher average earnings for women.

Furthermore, official statistics indicate that the gap increases substantially with age, reaching 16.7% among employees aged between 50 and 59. Sectors in which senior roles are predominantly held by men, such as construction, aviation and finance, consequently tend to exhibit wider gaps.

Nevertheless, Michelle McDonagh of the HR consultancy Adare emphasises that the figure does not measure equal pay for identical work, which is already a legal requirement. Instead, it primarily reflects the representation of women at senior levels.
